name: veterans-foreclosure-crisis-registers
title: Veterans Foreclosure Crisis, the registers of record
description: The claims, sources, chronology, rebuttals, dated record and glossary that the public-interest oversight project at veteransforeclosurecrisis.org is built from. Every claim carries an identifier, the source it rests on, the date it was last checked, and a stated limitation.

resources.name: claims
resources.title: Claims register
resources.description: Every factual claim on the site, what it rests on, and what it does not prove.

fields.name: claim_id
fields.description: Stable identifier, C plus three digits. Cited from the site as the C-number and never reused.

fields.name: claim_text
fields.description: The claim exactly as the site states it.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description: One or more source ids, semicolon separated.

fields.name: content_label
fields.description: Which tier of the claim system this belongs to. Governs how it is rendered and how strongly it may be stated.

fields.name: definition
fields.description: What the label means, carried inline so a downloaded CSV explains its own vocabulary.

fields.name: limitation
fields.description: What stops the figure being carried further than the document behind it can hold. Never blank.

fields.name: last_verified
fields.description: Date a human last checked this claim against its sources. ISO 8601.

fields.name: pages
fields.description: Semicolon separated page slugs where the claim is used editorially. Pages that render the whole claims register, The Record and Evidence, are NOT listed here; this field records where the claim is argued, not where the register is displayed. KNOWN INCOMPLETE, 2026-08-13: the slug vocabulary across all 58 rows is legacy-derived and no row recorded the Data and Methods or Latest pages until C010 was filled, which almost certainly means the column is under-maintained rather than that no other claim appears there. Treat a value here as a floor, not a complete list.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description: Stable identifier, S plus three digits. Cited from the site as the S-number and never reused.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The title of the document this row points to, as the document itself gives it. Not a description and not a URL slug.

fields.name: publisher
fields.description: The organisation that published the document, not the platform that hosts it.

fields.name: url
fields.description: An absolute URL, or a relative path to a captured PDF in the repo's docs/ folder. Nothing else. A field shift on 2026-08-09 put prose here and it stayed live for three days.

fields.name: pub_date
fields.description: ISO date, year-month, or year. Blank allowed.

fields.name: last_verified
fields.description: Date a human last confirmed the URL resolves and is the right document. ISO 8601.

fields.name: type
fields.description: What kind of document it is: analysis, press release, hearing record, statute, regulation, circular, news, advocacy org, and so on.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Verification state. 'verified': the URL resolves, it is the document named in the title, and pub_date is established or explicitly 'not dated'. 'verified-needs-url': the row is real and checked, but the URL currently held points at a related page rather than the document the title names. Replace the URL, do not delete the row. 'verified-needs-date': the URL is confirmed as the right document; publication date not yet established. 'registered-needs-title-and-date': auto-registered from a URL, so the title is a slug derived from that URL and is not the document's real title. 'held': under a hold order, must not be cited until released. 'unverified': registered but never checked. 'dead-no-archive': the URL no longer resolves AND no web archive capture exists, so this citation cannot be checked by anyone. Keep the row as a record of what was once cited, move live citations to a verifiable source, and never cite it externally.

fields.name: status_display
fields.title: Reader-facing label
fields.description: What a reader sees for this status. status is operational; this is public. Kept in the register rather than in a script so no tool can mistake the difference for drift.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Free text. Anything a reader needs in order to use this source correctly, including any figure the row is cited for.

fields.name: archived_url
fields.description: Web archive capture of the same document, so the citation survives link rot.

vfcRules.name: needs-date means no date yet
vfcRules.message: status says the date is not established, so pub_date must be empty. If the date is now known, set status to verified.

vfcRules.name: needs-title-and-date means no date yet
vfcRules.message: status says title and date are both outstanding, so pub_date must be empty.

vfcRules.name: verified means dated
vfcRules.message: a verified source carries a publication date, or the literal string 'not dated' where it has been established that the document has none.

resources.name: timeline
resources.title: Chronology
resources.description: The dated spine. The Record owns it; other pages render filtered views.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable identifier, T plus three digits.

fields.name: date
fields.description: Machine-sortable event date, ISO 8601.

fields.name: date_display
fields.description: The date as it should be shown to a reader, which may be less precise than the sort date.

fields.name: event
fields.description: What happened, in one sentence, stated as a dated fact.

fields.name: layer
fields.description: Which chronology view owns this entry. The Record owns the full spine; other pages render filtered views.

fields.name: span
fields.description: For events covering a period rather than a day, the period covered.

fields.name: who_was_told
fields.description: The party that received notice, where the entry is a notice event. Supports the foreseeability argument.

fields.name: who_told_them
fields.description: The party that gave notice.

fields.name: venue
fields.description: Where it happened: a hearing, a letter, a filing, a call, a published document.

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: Link to the record for this event.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description: WARN ONLY. Some rows carry a citation string rather than an S-id. Reconciling these is an open board item, so this warns and does not block.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Verification state of the entry.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Free text qualifier, including any registered limitation.

resources.name: rebuttals
resources.title: Rebuttal index
resources.description: What you may have heard, and what the record says.

fields.name: pr_id
fields.description: Stable identifier, PR plus two digits. PR numbering wins; the retired R-nn scheme is not used.

fields.name: group
fields.description: Which family of talking point this answers.

fields.name: strategy_code
fields.description: A strategy number and its name, e.g. 'R1 Tried-but-blocked'.

fields.name: heard
fields.description: The claim as a reader is likely to have heard it, in that speaker's own framing.

fields.name: where
fields.description: Where that claim has actually been made, with enough detail to check.

fields.name: record_says
fields.description: What the documented record shows, stated neutrally.

fields.name: authority
fields.description: The statute, regulation, circular or record that carries the answer.

fields.name: receipt
fields.description: The captured image or document that shows it on the face of the record.

fields.name: say_back
fields.description: A short reply a family member can use verbatim.

fields.name: if_again
fields.description: What to say if the claim is repeated after being answered.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Publication state of this entry, including whether it is held pending a receipt.

fields.name: last_verified
fields.description: Date a human last checked this entry against its authority. ISO 8601.

fields.name: origin
fields.description: Where this entry came from, so a merged entry can be traced back.

fields.name: anchor
fields.description: The in-page anchor this entry renders at, so a citation can point at it.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Free text, including any registered limitation.

resources.name: news
resources.title: The dated record
resources.description: Hearings, letters, program events and press items with external sources.

vfcRules.name: placeholder-url-stays-flagged
vfcRules.message: The literal 'URL pending' is the only placeholder allowed in url, and only while status is needs-url. If the status has moved to verified, the placeholder is stale.

fields.name: date
fields.description: Date of the item, ISO 8601.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Headline as the source itself gives it. Not paraphrased.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Hearing, letter, program event, press item, or agency action.

fields.name: url
fields.description: An absolute URL, or the literal placeholder 'URL pending' while status is needs-url. See vfcRules.

fields.name: source_org
fields.description: Publisher or the body that produced the item.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Verification state, including whether a URL is still being chased.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Free text qualifier.

resources.name: glossary
resources.title: Glossary
resources.description: Acronyms and terms spelled out on first use.

fields.name: term
fields.description: The acronym or term as it appears in the record.

fields.name: definition
fields.description: Plain-language expansion, written for a reader meeting the term for the first time.
